derived: LLY turned 14.30% of revenue into free cash over 2018 to 2025 against the 38.1% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: LLY paid $3,152mm of interest inside operating cash flow over 2018 to 2025, 1.17% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 28.46% to 27.30%. Restated at replacement capex: LLY spent $23,144mm on plant over 2018 to 2025 against $7,255mm of plant depreciation, 5.89% of revenue above what keeps the plant running. Taken at depreciation, the charge falls from 27.30% to 20.25%. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Restated without working capital build: over 2018 to 2025 LLY's cash flow statement shows receivables up $15,658mm, inventories up $10,223mm, payables and accrued liabilities up $18,257mm, a working capital build of $7,624mm, 2.83% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 20.25% to 16.87%.

column11: ANCHOR, pregabalin, the last new mechanism to reach DPNP with a measured share: of 12,074 US adults first diagnosed with DPN over 2006 to 2011 who started a DPNP medicine, 21.6% started pregabalin (Yang M, Qian C, Liu Y, Pain Med 2015;16(11):2075-2083, PMID 26118704, MarketScan). Lyrica was approved on 2004-12-30 (openFDA NDA021446, original), so the cohort spans its first years on sale. It is read here as a peak, which is conservative: Lyrica's revenue kept climbing after 2011, from $3,693mm to $4,595mm in 2013 (Pfizer FY2013 10-K exhibit 13, 0000078003-14-000018). MULTIPLE 0.25, A JUDGEMENT: 0.25 x 21.6% = 5.4% of the pool on the drug, close to the 5.2% of the same starts that duloxetine took while it was a branded, DPNP-labelled drug. The pool is each year's cohort and the stock carries at 25.5% a year, so the steady stock is peak x pool / 0.745, and a stock of 5.4% needs a peak of 0.054 x 0.745 = 0.04023. That takes pregabalin's stopping as the market's (74.5% against about 77%, Schuster et al. 2026), so its share of starts is its share of users. For more: the first AT2R antagonist, a peripheral non-opioid mechanism aimed at the tolerability that makes 56.3% of starters stop within 3 months (Schuster et al.). Against: it would launch in 2033 into a market where 59.0% of starts are generic gabapentin, pregabalin and duloxetine are generic, and suzetrigine gets there first; and the last AT2R antagonist, EMA401, missed significance in DPN (-0.6 on the NRS against placebo, P=0.10, 137 of 400 planned patients) before preclinical liver toxicity stopped it (Rice ASC et al., Pain 2021;162(10):2578-2589, PMID 33675631)
column12: the 0.25 multiple is the most arguable figure here; at 0.5, half pregabalin's share, revenue doubles. Nothing else claims this pool, so no crowding applies
